Help

How LaneLab works.

Recording a game

Choose the hand and ball, select the pins knocked down for each throw, then save. The scorecard updates as you go.

Pin tracking and notation

Tap a pin to mark it knocked down. A strike is X, a spare is /, and a gutter is −. Circles identify split pin leaves when applicable.

Bowling rules
Frames and scoring

A game has 10 frames. Frames 1–9 allow up to two deliveries. An open frame scores the pins knocked down; its running total includes that frame only.

Strikes and spares

A strike (X) knocks down all 10 pins on the first delivery and earns 10 plus the next two deliveries. A spare (/) clears the rack in two deliveries and earns 10 plus the next delivery.

Tenth-frame bonuses

A strike in frame 10 earns two bonus deliveries; a spare earns one. Bonus deliveries are scored in frame 10 and do not start an 11th frame.

Fouls, gutters, and pin totals

A foul counts as zero pins for that delivery. A gutter ball also records zero pins. Each delivery can knock down 0–10 pins, and the second delivery cannot exceed the pins left after the first.

Legal game limits

A complete game is scored from 0 to 300. A perfect game is 12 consecutive strikes: 10 strikes plus the two frame-10 bonus deliveries.

Editing a frame or game

Select a frame on the scorecard to edit its throws. Save the edit to recalculate that frame and all later totals; cancel leaves the saved game unchanged.

Importing and exporting

Use a CSV or JSON file from onboarding or Profile. JSON preserves the complete game structure; CSV is spreadsheet-friendly and includes frame, pin, hand, ball, and ball-rate columns.

Invalid files are rejected without replacing existing games.

Deleting data safely

Reset game clears only the current game. Reset entire app clears LaneLab’s profile, arsenal, games, and session data, then opens onboarding again.

Export your data first. Deletion cannot be undone without a backup.

Need a reminder while scoring?

The score screen labels the current frame and ball, and the pin tracker explains what to tap. Return here anytime from Profile → Help & how to use.
